    AI Overview
    +10
    The 152nd Kentucky Derby will take place on Saturday, May 2, 2026, at Churchill Downs in Louisville, KY, as the pinnacle of Derby Week starting April 25. The race features a 20-horse field qualifying through a points system. Early 2026 contenders include Renegade (4-1), Commandment (7-1), and The Puma (12-1). 
    Key 2026 Kentucky Derby Details: 
    • Date: Saturday, May 2, 2026.
    • Location: Churchill Downs, Louisville, KY.
    • Race: 152nd Running (Grade I).
    • Post Time: Typically around 6:57 p.m. ET (often shown on NBC).
    • Event Week: April 25 – May 2, 2026 (includes Kentucky Oaks on May 1st). 
    Top 2026 Contenders & Betting Outlook
    Early futures and analysis indicate a competitive field, with several horses emerging from top prep races: 
    • Renegade: Early favorite at 4-1.
    • Commandment: Considered a top contender after key historical angles (7-1).
    • The Puma: A major contender trained by Gustavo Delgado (12-1).
    • Chief Wallabee & Emerging Market: Other top-listed prospects. 
    Tickets and Attendance 
    • Tickets: Official ticket packages, including premium hospitality access, are available through Derby Experiences.
    • Travel Packages: Options include hotel accommodations and transit.
    • Simulcast: Other tracks, such as the Meadowlands Racetrack, offer viewing and wagering. 
    Preparation and Qualifying
    The field is determined by the "Road to the Kentucky Derby," a series of prep races. Key contenders have been training locally at Churchill Downs ahead of the event. 
    (Note: The 2026 Kentucky Derby results will be updated here after the race on May 2, 2026.)

    AI Overview
    The 2026 Kentucky Derby, running May 2nd, centers on historic traditions: sipping Mint Juleps, wearing elaborate hats, singing "My Old Kentucky Home," and honoring winners with the Rose Garland. Other traditions include Dawn at the Downs, the Oaks "Pink Out," and the "Run for the Roses" nickname. 
    Key 2026 Kentucky Derby Traditions
    • The Garland of Roses:
      The winner is draped in a garland of over 400 roses, giving the race its nickname, "Run for the Roses". 
    • Mint Julep:
      The official cocktail, featuring bourbon, sugar, mint, and crushed ice, served in commemorative cups. 
    • Derby Hats:
      Attendees wear stylish, often dramatic, hats to bring good luck and showcase fashion. 
    • "My Old Kentucky Home":
      Sung by the University of Louisville Marching Band as horses parade to the post. 
    • Kentucky Oaks Day ("Pink Out"):
      The Friday before the Derby, focused on fillies and breast cancer awareness with a Survivor's Parade. 
    • Dawn at the Downs:
      Morning workouts at Churchill Downs where fans watch contenders and enjoy breakfast. 
    • Celebrity Sightings:
      High-profile guests from sports, entertainment, and politics walk the red carpet. 
    • The Twin Spires:
      The race takes place under the iconic grandstand architecture at Churchill Downs. 
    Synonyms/Phrases for the Kentucky Derby Traditions 
    • The Run for the Roses®
    • The Most Exciting Two Minutes in Sports®
    • America's Race
    • Lilies for the Fillies: (Oaks Day)
    • The Fastest Two Minutes in Sports
    2026 Event Specifics 
    • 152nd Running: May 2, 2026.
    • Opening Night: April 25, 2026.
    • Week Events: Including Dawn at the Downs (April 27).

        The 152nd Kentucky Derby is scheduled for Saturday, May 2, 2026, at Churchill Downs in Louisville, KY. The marquee race (12th race of the day) is scheduled for 6:57 p.m. ET. Gates open at 9:00 a.m. ET, with the first race starting at 11:00 a.m. ET. NBC and Peacock provide coverage. 
        Key 2026 Derby Week Details:
        • Kentucky Derby Day: Saturday, May 2, 2026 (Race at 6:57 p.m. ET). 
        • Kentucky Oaks Day: Friday, May 1, 2026 (Gates open 11:00 a.m. ET, First Race 12:30 p.m. ET). 
        • Opening Day: Saturday, April 25, 2026. 
        • TV Coverage: NBC and Peacock (2:30 p.m. – 7:30 p.m. ET). 
        Note: The Kentucky Derby traditionally takes place on the first Saturday in May.

          Qualifying Races. What are the qualifying races for the Kentucky Derby 2026?
          About this result

          AI Overview
          The 2026 Kentucky Derby qualifying races (the "Road to the Kentucky Derby") consist of a series of prep races offering points to the top five finishers, running from Sept. 2025 through early April 2026. Key final prep races in 2026 include the Florida Derby, Arkansas Derby, Wood Memorial, and Blue Grass Stakes. 
          Major 2026 Kentucky Derby Qualifying Races & Dates (Championship Series) 
          • Risen Star Stakes: Feb. 14, 2026 (Fair Grounds)
          • Gotham Stakes: Feb. 28, 2026 (Aqueduct)
          • Rebel Stakes: March 1, 2026 (Oaklawn Park)
          • San Felipe Stakes: March 7, 2026 (Santa Anita)
          • Louisiana Derby: March 21, 2026 (Fair Grounds)
          • Arkansas Derby: March 28, 2026 (Oaklawn Park)
          • Florida Derby: March 28, 2026 (Gulfstream Park)
          • Wood Memorial: April 4, 2026 (Aqueduct)
          • Blue Grass Stakes: April 4, 2026 (Keeneland)
          • Santa Anita Derby: Early April 2026
          Other Qualifying Races (Prep Season & Early 2026) 
          • Iroquois Stakes: Sept. 13, 2025 (Churchill Downs - start of season)
          • Jerome Stakes: Jan. 3, 2026 (Aqueduct)
          • Lecomte Stakes: Jan. 17, 2026 (Fair Grounds)
          • UAE 2000 Guineas: Jan. 23, 2026 (Meydan)
          • Holy Bull Stakes: Jan. 31, 2026 (Gulfstream)
          • Southwest Stakes: Late Jan/Feb 2026 (Oaklawn)
          International Pathways 
          • Japan Road: Includes the Fukuryu Stakes.
          • Euro/Mideast Road: Includes the UAE Derby.
          Qualifying Race Synonyms & Usage 
          • Synonyms:
            Kentucky Derby Preps, Derby Trail, Road to the Derby, Triple Crown Preps (early stage), Championship Series Races.
          • Usage:
            These races are designed to test 3-year-old Thoroughbreds over increasing distances (from 1 mile to 1 1/8 miles) to prepare them for the 1 1/4-mile distance of the Kentucky Derby. Points (e.g., 100-50-25-15-10 in final races) decide the field limit of 20 starters.

            Rules. What are the rules of the Kentucky Derby 2026?
            About this result
            Feedback
            An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
            AI Overview
            The 2026 Kentucky Derby is restricted to 3-year-old Thoroughbreds (male or female) with a maximum of 20 starters determined by a points-based qualification system on the "Road to the Kentucky Derby". Held May 2, 2026, at
            1141 and one-fourth
            miles, the race requires horses to earn spots through 36+ specific prep races, including Championship Series events in March and April.             
            Usage Examples & Key Rules (2026 Season):
            • Qualification: Horses earn points (e.g., 100-40-30-20-10 in key prep races) to make the top 20, with four additional "also-eligible" spots reserved. 
            • Nominations: Owners must pay a fee to nominate 3-year-olds to the Triple Crown series. 
            • Structure: The race is a 1.25-mile sprint on dirt, limited to 3-year-olds. 
            • International Spots: Separate paths exist for Japan (1 bid) and Europe/Middle East (2 bids), with new races in Saudi Arabia and Dubai included for 2026. 
            • Weights: Colts and geldings carry 126 pounds, while fillies carry 121 pounds. 
            Synonyms/Related Terms of the Rules: 
            • Entry Conditions: The eligibility criteria and nomination requirements.
            • Qualifying Structure: The points system for the "Road to the Derby".
            • Field Limitations: The 20-horse maximum starter rule.
            • Race Conditions: The 3-year-old age restriction and distance.
            For 2026, the main Road to the Derby consisted of 36 races, and the top 20 points-earners generally guarantee a spot. The Kentucky Derby Draw Day is set for April 25, 2026, to finalize the field.
